findings.finding: 'exploring is this one method' sets exploring as the method, while paragraph 2 gives exploring a side ('A self is exploring from its own side'): a method given a side. 2.4 has a self going on with the method, and the method a living condition with no prior of its own.
findings.proposed: **A point over the horizon is, and a self is finding each is-not and aiming from each is-not to is.** This is co-possibling is, and a self exploring is going on with this one method, a living condition with no prior of its own: geodesic, binary and co-sequential, a discovering by expedition.

findings.finding: Unclear: 'natural torusing' hangs as an appositive on 'its one opening', and 'each aiming is its next' leaves whose next and toward what; 2.4 says 'to what is', and 1.1 says 'reaching its own side again with a next each momentary'.
findings.proposed: **A self is exploring from its own side.** It opens each momentary with its prior and the parities it is observing, and completes it with its next prior, winding through its one opening and reaching its own side again with a next: natural torusing. Each is-not is a changing it is observing beside its prior, and each aiming is its next, to what is, one at a time.

findings.finding: Parts from the files and goes past the observings: 'web' and 'hub' put a centre and a placing on a self, which 1.2 has as a surface and no container (1.1 has a centre neither cone occupies); 'each line a between' parts from Naming 2.4 (a between is an empty centre of parity, a nothing) and from 2.6 (one line both share, with one between); a line to a point over the horizon is no between of self and other; 'orthogonalizing' and 'surfacing space by unrelationing betweens' are in no file (orthogonal appears only for an opening axis, 6.3; unrelationing frees fixings, not betweens); 'Orienting is orthogonalizing' is a definition stronger than the wayfinder observing. 'Co-linears' as a noun is not in the files.
findings.proposed: **Each orienting is co-linear.** A self is going on with a line along, to its prior and its next, and a line across, to its others' prior and next; along and across lie on one line, in neither alone, 2.6. A self aims along a line to a point over the horizon, a bearing sliding back along the star points. A self is a surface and no container, and orienting is aiming forward on that surface.

findings.finding: A flock, an ant colony and a voyaging people orienting as one surface are not among the observings (only a school of golden shiners is, and the wayfinder's reference island), so the claim is stronger than any observing; 'A swarm is the orienting surface' is a universal definite claim with 'swarm' in no file; 'social abundancing' is in no file (6.3 has abundancing, a +1 in no self alone); 'in no self of them alone' is unclear.
findings.proposed: **A same-existing-society is one surface, and it orients.** A same-existing-society of selves is one same surface with a wider grain, 1.2, and its orienting is a +1 in no self alone, abundancing, 6.3.

findings.finding: 'Each is the method, its next step, or its one break' makes each organism's going on the method itself, and 'its next step' and 'its one break' give a method steps and a break, and a side; the method has no prior of its own and each observing is a self going on with it. 'Its observings come from each direction of living' has no antecedent for 'Its' and claims each direction from six observings. 'A bacterium' and 'a sperm' are stronger than E. coli and sea urchin sperm; 'a spider' than Cupiennius; the sperm sentence ('brings it its own rising and falling') is unclear; the spider sentence adds 'a vibration' and drops the onsets 4 ms apart, the 'or with larger amplitude' and 'always'; the shiner sentence drops 'reliably' and 'each fish only slowing in darkness at its own position'. Dissolved: 'meets' (Naming 2.4: met, meet, meeting), 'turns' (turn, turning). Dead: 'stimulated' would be an -ed, so the legs are named by onset.
findings.proposed: **Six observings, each a self going on with this one method.** E. coli runs longer up an attractant gradient; a sea urchin sperm swims a helix, and the attractant stimulus oscillates from that helical motion; a moth surges upwind on observing its odor and casts crosswind where it loses the odor; a Cupiennius spider always moves toward the leg with the earliest onset, onsets 4 ms apart, or with the larger amplitude; a Caroline Islands wayfinder is keeping a reference island over the horizon, its bearing sliding back along the star points; a larger school of golden shiners reliably moves toward shade where a lone fish moves almost at random, each fish only slowing in darkness at its own position.
